auth.description: Slack bot user OAuth token (xoxb-…) with chat:write, channels:history, users:read and reactions:write
auth.name: slack.bot_token
auth.subject: app

auth.description: Slack app signing secret, used to verify inbound Events API requests. Never sent to Slack
auth.name: slack.signing_secret
auth.subject: app

channels.description: Socket Mode — flux opens an outbound WebSocket and Slack pushes events down it. No public URL, and no signature: the connection is authenticated by the app-level token that opened it
channels.name: socket

channels.description: The Events API — Slack POSTs to an endpoint the operator exposes, signing each request. Use it when an outbound WebSocket is not an option; it needs a public URL and the signing secret
channels.name: events-api

steps: Open your app at api.slack.com/apps, or create one for this workspace
Under Event Subscriptions, turn on Enable Events
Paste the Request URL shown above and wait for Slack's `url_verification` challenge to pass
Under Subscribe to bot events, add the events you selected here
Copy the Signing Secret from Basic Information into this connection's signing secret field
Reinstall the app to the workspace so the new event scopes take effect

description: Slack messaging: post messages, read conversation history, look up users, react

events.description: Someone @-mentioned the app in a channel it is a member of
events.name: app_mention

events.description: A message was posted in a channel the app is a member of. Fires for every human message, so a program that triggers on it should expect volume
events.name: message

operations.description: Post a message to a Slack channel, visible to everyone in it. Slack answers HTTP 200 even on failure: check `ok` in the response body before treating the message as sent

params.description: Channel id (`C0123ABCDEF`) or name to post to. An id is preferred; a name resolves only for public channels
params.name: channel

params.description: Message text, in Slack's mrkdwn syntax
params.name: text

params.description: The `ts` of a parent message to reply to, threading the reply under it. Omit to post at channel level
params.name: thread_ts

channel.description: The channel the message landed in, always as an id (`C0123ABCDEF`) even when the request named it

error.description: Present only when `ok` is false: Slack's machine-readable failure code, such as `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel` or `msg_too_long`

message.description: The message as Slack stored it: `text`, `type`, `subtype`, `ts`, `bot_id`, `username`, and `attachments` when there are any

ok.description: False on failure, with HTTP still 200. Branch on this before reading anything else — it is the only member present in both outcomes

ts.description: The posted message's timestamp id, e.g. `1503435956.000247`. This is what addresses the message afterwards — `slack-reactions-add`'s `timestamp`, and `thread_ts` to reply under it

operations.description: Read recent messages from a Slack channel, newest first. Slack answers HTTP 200 even on failure: check `ok` in the response body, where an error such as `channel_not_found` appears at `error`

params.description: Maximum messages to return in one call, newest first. Slack's documented maximum is 999 and it advises far less
params.name: limit

params.description: Only messages after this `ts`, e.g. `1728394857.123456`. Omit for no lower bound
params.name: oldest

params.description: Only messages up to this `ts`. Omit for no upper bound
params.name: latest

error.description: Present only when `ok` is false: `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel` or `invalid_arguments`

has_more.description: True when the channel holds older messages than this page returned. This connector cannot page — see the header comment on the missing cursor — so a true here means the caller is seeing a window, not the history

messages.description: The messages, newest first. Each carries at least `type`, `ts` and `text`; a user message also carries `user`, and a bot or system message carries a `subtype` instead

ok.description: False on failure, with HTTP still 200. Branch on this first

response_metadata.description: Carries `next_cursor`, the cursor for the following page. It cannot be sent back by this connector (C-30)

operations.description: Look up one Slack user by id — display name, real name, time zone and whether they are a bot. Slack answers HTTP 200 even on failure: check `ok` in the response body, where an error such as `user_not_found` appears at `error`

error.description: Present only when `ok` is false: typically `user_not_found`

ok.description: False on failure, with HTTP still 200. Branch on this first

user.description: The user: `id`, `team_id`, `name`, `real_name`, `deleted`, `tz`, `tz_label`, `tz_offset`, `is_bot`, `is_admin`, `is_owner`, `updated`, and `profile` — which holds the display name, status and, with `users:read.email`, the email address

operations.description: Add an emoji reaction to a message, visible to everyone in the channel. Slack answers HTTP 200 even on failure: check `ok` in the response body, where an error such as `already_reacted` appears at `error`

params.description: The `ts` of the message to react to, e.g. `1728394857.123456`
params.name: timestamp

params.description: Emoji name without colons, e.g. `thumbsup` or `white_check_mark`
params.name: name

error.description: Present only when `ok` is false, with HTTP still 200: `already_reacted`, `message_not_found`, `invalid_name`, `channel_not_found` or `thread_locked`

ok.description: True when the reaction was added. There is no other member on success — Slack returns no id for a reaction
